title: Stem cells; Cell specialisation, tissues, organs
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE07a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE08b#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE07a#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE08b#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE07a#N.3a, CE08b#N.5, CE07a#N.10b, CE08b#N.8, CE07a#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Zygote
items.clue: The single cell from which a whole body is built up by mitosis

items.label: Adult stem cells
items.clue: Found in bone marrow, for example; make a limited range of types and can come from the patient

items.label: Differentiation
items.clue: Process in which a cell gains a structure suited to one function, by switching on certain genes

items.label: Embryonic stem cells
items.clue: Taken from the inner mass of an early IVF spare, which is destroyed; can form any type of body tissue

questions.stem: In a human, a neuron and a liver cell are both descended by mitosis from the same zygote. What is the difference between them once they have differentiated?

options.text: They express different subsets of the same complete set of genes.
They have kept different sets of genes and discarded the rest.
They were set on different paths inside from fertilisation.
They differ only until the body needs to swap them over.

questions.explanation: All cells produced by mitosis from the zygote inherit the full genome. The neuron switches on the genes for its proteins and the liver cell a different set, while both keep every gene.

questions.stem: Bone marrow transplants are used to treat leukaemia. Which statement explains how a transplant replaces the patient's blood cells?

options.text: The donor marrow's stem cells can become any body cell, so they replace any damaged tissue.
Mature red blood cells in the donor marrow divide to make all the new blood cells.
Donor stem cells divide and differentiate to give every type of blood cell.
Donor white blood cells switch into red blood cells when the patient needs more.

questions.explanation: Blood stem cells renew themselves and differentiate into red cells, white cells and platelet-forming cells, rebuilding the patient's blood supply.

questions.stem: The wall of the stomach contains epithelium, smooth muscle and connective tissue. Together they digest and churn food. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Epithelium, muscle and connective tissue are each organs, as each has a function.
The stomach is an organ system, as it contains several different tissues.
The stomach is an organ: several tissues working together for an overall function.
Epithelium is not a tissue if it contains goblet cells as well as other cells.

questions.explanation: Epithelium, muscle and connective tissue each do one job; together they perform digestion, the stomach's overall function.

questions.stem: Which of these is a question that scientific evidence alone cannot answer?

options.text: Do neurons made from iPS cells survive after transplant into the brain?
Should human embryos be used to make stem cells for research?
How often do treatments using embryonic stem cells cause tumours?
Are a patient's own iPS cells rejected less often than donor cells?

questions.explanation: "Should" asks about values. Evidence informs the answer, but society decides it.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species of plant, leaf cells make large amounts of a protein that binds chlorophyll, but the root cells of the same plant make none of it. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: In root cells, the base sequence of the gene has been changed, and the gene no longer codes for the protein.
Both cell types carry the gene for the protein, but it is expressed in leaf cells and not in root cells.
Root cells have lost the gene for the protein from their DNA because they did not use it.
Root cells do not need the protein, so they choose not to make it, unlike the cells of leaves.
